- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.5) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak values by 5–10%.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >10% from prior day), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at 1–2 days above true peak.
- If sentiment turns negative (≤0.3) mid-period, model frequently underestimates downward trend; add 2–5% downward bias to forecast.
- Model exhibits strong mean reversion bias: if 3+ consecutive days show price decline, forecast should not rise above prior 3-day average.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overweights early sentiment (first 5–7 days) and underweights later sentiment; weight sentiment decay exponentially (e.g., 0.9^day_offset).
- When sentiment is mixed (0.3–0.7), model tends to average sentiment; use sentiment-weighted moving average for smoothing.
- If true outcome shows “double dip” or “rebound after dip”, model often misses the second leg; add 1–2% upward bias in second half of forecast.
- Model underestimates true price volatility in high-sentiment periods; increase forecast standard deviation by 10–15% if sentiment >0.6 for 3+ consecutive days.
